interactions.prompt: How can I set HSV thresholds to distinguish white lane markings from grey road surfaces when their brightness is very similar?
interactions.response:
When the brightness of the white lane and the grey road is very similar, using only the V (brightness) channel is usually not enough. Instead, I would look at both Saturation (S) and Value (V). White pixels normally have low saturation because they contain relatively little colour, while grey road pixels can have slightly different saturation values.

A practical approach is to first sample some pixels from the white lane and grey road, then compare their HSV values. Based on these values, choose a threshold range rather than guessing it. For example, you could use a relatively low S threshold to keep pixels that are close to white, together with a suitable V range to remove darker road areas.

interactions.prompt: Why does cv2.inRange() sometimes detect parts of the grey road as white lane markings?
interactions.response: cv2.inRange() only checks whether each pixel is inside the HSV range you provide. If some grey road pixels have HSV values that fall inside that range, they will also become part of the mask. This can happen when the road is bright or the lighting changes. The solution is not just to make the threshold smaller blindly. It is better to inspect the false-positive pixels, adjust the S and V limits, and then use later processing such as morphology and ROI to remove some remaining noise.

interactions.prompt: If only one lane is detected, how can I estimate the missing lane without making the result unstable?
interactions.response: When only one side is detected, I would avoid creating the missing lane from a completely fixed position every frame. A better approach for this project is to use the detected lane together with the previous centreline or previous lane information. The missing side can be estimated using the expected road width. If previous information is not available, a fixed default road width can be used as a fallback. This gives the detector a reasonable result even when one lane temporarily disappears.

interactions.prompt: How can I reduce the processing time of my lane detection pipeline without changing the main detection method?
interactions.response: I would first identify which part of the pipeline is taking the most time instead of changing everything at once. Some practical options are reducing the input resolution, limiting the ROI before expensive processing, avoiding unnecessary image copies, and only calculating the information needed by the controller. Since the pipeline uses several image-processing steps, processing a smaller relevant region can reduce the amount of work while keeping the same overall method.

interactions.prompt: Why can the car move very slowly in Webots even when the lane detection itself seems to work?
interactions.response: The slow movement may not come from lane detection alone. The controller may contain speed limiting logic, or the perception pipeline may be taking too long between control updates. Other simulator or model components can also add processing time. I would first check the controller's speed command and any speed limits, then measure how often the control loop is running. After that, I would check whether perception, object detection or segmentation is using most of the processing time.

interactions.prompt: How should I choose Canny edge detection thresholds for our lane detection images?
interactions.response: There is no single correct pair of Canny thresholds for every image. The values should be chosen based on the contrast between the lane edges and the road. I would start with a reasonable low/high pair, inspect the edge image, and then adjust it. If there are too many noisy edges, the thresholds can be made more restrictive. If the lane edges disappear, the thresholds may need to be relaxed. The important thing is to evaluate the output on the actual project images rather than choosing values only from an example online.

interactions.prompt: Why can my lane detection work on saved images but behave differently when it is integrated with Webots?
interactions.response: The saved test images and Webots camera frames may not have exactly the same conditions. Differences can come from image resolution, colour format, lighting, camera position, frame timing or preprocessing. The first thing I would check is the actual image shape and format received from Webots and compare it with the images used during testing. Then I would inspect the intermediate HSV mask, Canny result and Hough result to find where the behaviour starts to change.

interactions.prompt: What should my lane detector return when neither lane is detected?
interactions.response: It is better not to invent a completely new lane position when there is no reliable detection. The detector can first try to use the previous valid centreline or previous lane information. If that is also unavailable, it can use a defined fallback based on the expected road width and image geometry. The important part is that the output format stays consistent so the navigation module can still handle the result.
